topic: SAA multi-station decay — post-patch verification of ISS-2602–2606 (c3 5-patch set)
our_argument_summary: WIN-041 (verdict: Misleading) argues the dome's five-station SAA decay claim is (1) one regional observation counted five times — correlated samples of a single anomaly, not independent confirmations; (2) circular, because the ≥28 nT/yr threshold is a model input, not a derived prediction; (3) post-hoc, with no monitor.py coverage; and (4) the dome's newer boundary-zone-decay framing fails because standard reversed-flux-patch models predict the spatial structure while the dome's axisymmetric H(r) cannot produce any azimuthal structure at all.

The flagged sentence was replaced verbatim with the recommended breakdown (CHAOS-7 2000-2025 / WMM2025 2024-2025 / direct pulls 2022-2024). But the untouched lead-in clause of the SAME paragraph still asserts 'the same observatory network, station coverage, and time windows used across WIN-004, WIN-005, WIN-035, and WIN-037' — the original overclaim, now directly contradicted by the corrected sentence that follows it. See holes 2 and 3.

The rebuttal paragraph itself is strong and correctly argues both prongs (standard models predict the spatial structure; the dome's axisymmetric H(r) derives nothing).

dome_code_analysis.calculation_pipeline: Dome page WIN-041 presents a five-station table (TDC -79.7, SHE -54.2, HER -45.3, PST -38.8, KOU -31.0 nT/yr) sourced 'Direct HAPI pulls 2022-2024', registered 2026-03-15. monitor.py contains NO domain for this five-station claim. The only SAA-decay domain (Domain 8, lines 489-497) covers single-station Tsumeb/TTB with hardcoded predicted=77.0/observed=77.0, error_pct 0.0, pass:True — a display, not a validation. The >=28 nT/yr threshold is a model input (05-model.txt line 42: 'Field decay rate: >=28 nT/year').
dome_code_analysis.hardcoded_vs_computed: The five-station claim is entirely outside the monitoring suite; the adjacent Domain 8 check is a pred==obs identity with pass hardcoded True. Nothing about WIN-041 is computed at validation time.
data_sources_used: INTERMAGNET HAPI (claimed by dome page for the five stations)
INTERMAGNET TTB annual means (Domain 8 label only)
dome_code_analysis.escape_clauses: Domain 8 carries tolerance_pct 20.0 but pass is literal True, so tolerance is decorative.
dome_code_analysis.code_discrepancies: None found this cycle. Our disambiguated text (Domain 8 single-station hardcoded identity; no domain covers the five-station claim) matches monitor.py exactly. Nit: the Domain 8 label string reads '> 28 nT/yr' where our text says '≥28 nT/yr' — immaterial.

code_analysis_tags.monitoring_evidence: Re-verified against monitor.py sha 9de912a86 (unchanged since c3): grep for TDC/Tristan/SHE/Kourou/Stanley/Hermanus station codes returns nothing; no domain aggregates multi-station SAA data. Domain 8 (lines 489-497) is single-station TTB hardcoded 77.0/77.0 and belongs to the WIN-015/WIN-037 claim family per its own source label ('INTERMAGNET TTB annual means (WIN-015)').
code_analysis_tags.relabels_standard_evidence: SAA decay rates and their spatial structure are outputs of standard field models (CHAOS-7, WMM secular variation); the published mechanism is reversed-flux-patch growth at the CMB (Terra-Nova et al. 2017, doi:10.1016/j.pepi.2017.03.002). The dome relabels the cause 'aetheric field separation' while adopting observed station values.
code_analysis_tags.post_hoc_evidence: Dome page prints 'Registered: 2026-03-15 | Source: Direct HAPI pulls 2022-2024' on adjacent lines (02-wins.txt lines 444-445, poll 2026-06-06) — the confirming data window closed ~15 months before registration. The dome's own metadata concedes the sequence.
code_analysis_tags.derives_from_dome_evidence: The 'aetheric field separation predicts maximum decay at the inter-cell boundary' line (02-wins.txt line 456) is asserted with no derivation; the dome's field equation H(r)=8537·exp(−r/8619) (05-model.txt lines 16, 33) is a function of radial distance only and cannot produce azimuthal structure. The >=28 threshold is a model input (05-model.txt line 42).

holes_found.description: WRONG DOI introduced by the ISS-2603 patch. detail_verdict_text cites 'Terra-Nova et al. 2017' with href https://doi.org/10.1093/gji/ggx374 — that DOI resolves to Katou et al. 2018, 'Reciprocal data acquisition and subsequent waveform matching for integrated onshore-offshore seismic profiling', Geophysical Journal International 212(1):509-521 (verified via Crossref this run). A seismic-profiling paper with zero relevance to the SAA. The correct DOI is 10.1016/j.pepi.2017.03.002 ('Relating the South Atlantic Anomaly and geomagnetic flux patches', Terra-Nova, Amit, Hartmann, Trindade & Pinheiro, Phys. Earth Planet. Inter. 2017) — already used correctly in WIN-004 and WIN-005. This repeats the WIN-008/009/014 wrong-DOI failure class on a freshly patched WIN; a defender who clicks the link can discredit the whole rebuttal paragraph.
holes_found.recommendation: One-line fix: replace href https://doi.org/10.1093/gji/ggx374 with https://doi.org/10.1016/j.pepi.2017.03.002 in WIN-041 detail_verdict_text. Run tests/citation checks after.

holes_found.description: TLDR factual error (carry-over descendant of c3 hole 0 / ISS-2602): tldr_verdict opens 'WIN-041 draws from the same stations as multiple earlier WINs.' Our own corrected detail_evidence now concedes the other WINs cite NO station lists — WIN-004/005 use the CHAOS-7 field model and WIN-037 uses WMM2025. The dome page names five specific stations for WIN-041 only. Readers see TLDRs first; a defender can falsify this sentence by quoting the dome's own source lines, exactly the attack the ISS-2602 patch was meant to close.
holes_found.recommendation: Change tldr_verdict first sentence to: 'WIN-041 repackages the same regional signal already counted in multiple earlier WINs.' (Keeps the simplification, drops the falsifiable station claim.)

holes_found.description: Residual overclaim in detail_evidence lead-in (carry-over descendant of c3 hole 0 / ISS-2602, which is now closed): the paragraph still opens '...the same observatory network, station coverage, and time windows used across WIN-004, WIN-005, WIN-035, and WIN-037', then the next sentence (the ISS-2602 patch) correctly says the windows merely OVERLAP and the sources differ (CHAOS-7 model vs WMM2025 vs direct pulls). The two sentences contradict each other inside one paragraph; 'station coverage, and time windows' restates the very overclaim the patch removed.
holes_found.recommendation: Trim the lead-in to: 'WIN-041 reprocesses INTERMAGNET SAA-region station data — the same observational basis underlying WIN-004, WIN-005, WIN-035, and WIN-037.' The corrected sentence that follows then carries the precise breakdown.

holes_found.description: Cross-WIN consistency: WIN-041's new rebuttal says the SAA's 'deepening and splitting is reproduced by growth of reversed-flux patches (Terra-Nova et al. 2017)', while WIN-005 — about the same paper — carefully hedges: Terra-Nova et al. 'relate the anomaly's structure and splitting to reversed-flux patches... characterising the patch dynamics rather than deriving a specific inter-cell decay-rate ratio.' A defender can quote our WIN-005 hedge against our WIN-041 claim. The companion assertion that 'CHAOS-7 secular-variation maps place the fastest decline precisely in the region between the separating cells' is uncited and 'precisely' overstates what an SV map shows.
holes_found.recommendation: Align with WIN-005's phrasing: 'standard models relate this spatial structure to reversed-flux-patch growth at the core-mantle boundary (Terra-Nova et al. 2017), and CHAOS-7 secular-variation maps show the strongest decline in the region between the separating cells.' Drop 'precisely'; optionally cite Finlay et al. 2020 (doi:10.1186/s40623-020-01252-9, already used in WIN-005) for the CHAOS-7 SV maps.

holes_found.description: tldr_verdict second sentence still leans on the threshold frame ISS-2605 abandoned: 'Stations within the SAA's spatial correlation length aren't independent.' The detail now argues independence fails 'regardless of pairwise distance'; the TLDR re-introduces the correlation-length criterion (numberless, so not directly falsifiable, but inconsistent with the reframe).
holes_found.recommendation: Rewrite tldr_verdict sentence 2: 'Correlated samples of one regional anomaly aren't independent confirmations — this is one observation counted multiple times.'

holes_found.description: detail_evidence conflates two locations of the >=28 threshold: 'the dome's own monitoring code hardcodes the validation threshold at ≥28 nT/year — a value... manually set in the model's configuration.' In fact the threshold lives in the model spec (05-model.txt line 42) and appears in monitoring code only inside Domain 8's label string (monitor.py line 492) — and Domain 8 isn't WIN-041's check anyway, as our own detail_verdict_text now explains. Both halves are individually true; fused they blur the precise (and stronger) point.
holes_found.recommendation: Rephrase: 'the ≥28 nT/yr threshold is a model input (set in the dome's own model specification, echoed in its monitoring labels), not a value derived from any dome-geometry equation.'

stronger_arguments.description: Still unadopted from c3: the dome's own registration metadata is the cleanest post-hoc proof. The live page prints 'Registered: 2026-03-15 | Source: Direct HAPI pulls 2022-2024' on adjacent lines — the confirming data window closed ~15 months before the prediction was registered. Our post-hoc paragraph still argues the weaker 'publicly available at the time of the dome monitor commit' + absent pre-registration line. Quoting the dome's own dates needs no timestamping argument at all.

The dome's own five-station table is azimuthal-structure evidence AGAINST its own axisymmetric field equation: graded rates from TDC -79.7 to KOU -31.0 across ~72 degrees of longitude cannot be produced by H(r)=8537·exp(−r/8619), which depends on radial distance only. Our rebuttal paragraph makes this point; it could be promoted into tldr_verdict where it is currently absent.

kernel_of_truth.description: The station data are real and the gradient is genuinely interesting: the dome's table (02-wins.txt lines 447-454, poll 2026-06-06) reports a coherent spatial gradient in decay rate — fastest at the inter-cell saddle (TDC -79.7 nT/yr) and slowest at the fringe (KOU -31.0 nT/yr) — and that pattern matches what CHAOS-7-era secular-variation analyses of the splitting SAA show (Terra-Nova et al. 2017, doi:10.1016/j.pepi.2017.03.002). The author also did real work pulling per-station HAPI series ('Direct HAPI pulls 2022-2024', 02-wins.txt line 445) rather than quoting a model summary.
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Real data, wrong inference, twice over. First, five correlated samples of one regional anomaly are one confirmation, not five (wins.json WIN-041 detail_verdict_text, this cycle's reframed paragraph 1). Second, the boundary-zone gradient the dome touts as dome-vs-globe evidence is azimuthal structure that the dome's own radial-only field equation H(r)=8537·exp(−r/8619) (05-model.txt line 16) is mathematically incapable of producing, while reversed-flux-patch models do produce it (Terra-Nova et al. 2017). The dome's strongest exhibit is self-undermining, and its registration metadata (02-wins.txt lines 444-445) concedes the post-hoc sequence.

deeper_analysis: This was a verification pass on the decider's 5-patch self-apply (commit d4fa543). Net assessment: 3 of 5 holes fully closed (ISS-2604, ISS-2605, ISS-2606), 1 substantively closed but with a critical regression (ISS-2603's rebuttal paragraph cites the wrong DOI — a seismic paper — for Terra-Nova et al. 2017), and 1 partially closed (ISS-2602's overclaim survives in the paragraph lead-in and in tldr_verdict). The verdict 'Misleading' is secure: the core argument is now stronger than at c3, the dome-vs-globe rebuttal is in place, and the correlation-length vulnerability is gone from the detail text. The critical DOI hole is a one-line fix but must be treated urgently — it sits inside the newest, most attack-worthy paragraph, and this project has prior history of wrong-DOI findings (WIN-008/009/014). Advocate-mode check: the strongest remaining defender move after the DOI fix would be 'your WIN-005 says Terra-Nova characterises rather than derives, your WIN-041 says reproduces — which is it?' (hole 4). Carry-over note: holes 2 and 3 restate parts of c3 hole 0; the matching ISS-2602 is already CLOSED, so no unresolved_prior_cycle entry is possible — decider should open a fresh ISS for the residual text (see summary_for_decider).
